definitions.explanation: The financial process of settling accounts, paying off debts, or dissolving a business by selling off its assets.

definitions.gloss: clearing up; settling (a relationship or past issue)
definitions.explanation: Figuratively, putting an end to a relationship, situation, or past issue by resolving it completely.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}を{清算|せいさん}する。
{借金|しゃっきん}の{清算|せいさん}に{時間|じかん}がかかった。
examples.english: It took time to settle the debts.

examples.japanese: {倒産|とうさん}した{企業|きぎょう}の{資産|しさん}を{清算|せいさん}する{手続|てつづ}きが{始|はじ}まった。
examples.english: The process of liquidating the assets of the bankrupt company has begun.

examples.japanese: {過去|かこ}を{清算|せいさん}する。
examples.english: To settle matters from the past.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}との{関係|かんけい}を{清算|せいさん}したい。
examples.english: I want to put an end to my relationship with him.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{因縁|いんねん}を{清算|せいさん}して、{新|あたら}しい{人生|じんせい}を{歩|あゆ}み{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: Having settled the long-standing grudge, I started walking a new path in life.

notes:
USAGE:
Often used with する to form the verb {清算|せいさん}する. Sense 1 is a financial/business term. Sense 2 is a figurative extension commonly used for ending relationships or resolving past issues.

NOTE: Not to be confused with {精算|せいさん} (fare adjustment, exact calculation) or {生産|せいさん} (production). All three are homophones.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {清算|せいさん}する (to settle, to liquidate)
- {過去|かこ}を{清算|せいさん}する (to settle the past)
- {会社|かいしゃ}の{清算|せいさん} (company liquidation)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {精算|せいさん}: fare adjustment, exact calculation — different meaning despite identical pronunciation
- {決済|けっさい}: settlement (of payment) — focuses on completing a transaction
